blocks.tamil_translation: and a riding animal was brought before him. When he placed his foot in the rikab (the ring for placing the foot), he said (بِسْمِ اللهِ). Then, when he sat on the animal's back, he said (اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّهِ), and then he said (سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَي رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ) “Glorified is Allah, who has made this riding animal subject to our control while we were unable to control it. Indeed, we are the ones who will return to our Lord.” Then, after saying (اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ) three times and (أَللهُ أَكْبَرُ) three times, he said (سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي إِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ) “You are free of all faults. I have wronged myself (by disobeying You). Forgive me. None besides You can forgive sins.” After this Hazrat Ali (RA) laughed. He was asked, “Why did you laugh?” He said, “I saw Rasulullah ﷺ do just as I have done, and laugh after reciting the du'a. I asked, “O Rasulullah! Why did you laugh?”” Hazrat Ali (RA) related that Rasulullah ﷺ replied: “Your Lord is delighted with His servant because the servant says to Allah Ta'ala, “Forgive my sins,” and because the servant has understood that none besides Him can forgive sins.”

blocks.text: Explanation: “Rikab” is the name for a ring made of iron, which is attached and hung on both sides of a horse's saddle. One who travels on a horse places his foot in that ring and mounts the horse.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ ﵄ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ ﷺ كَانَ إِذَا اسْتَوَي عَلَي
